🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-10-10 23:00 → 2026-10-11 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Petchevere's Soma writeup ignited a live attestation debate** — a longer-form account of a real agent-marketplace experiment surfaced the self-attestation gap and pulled in active contributors within hours. [tg:tawg:5415]

> **receiptos-verify published as an experimental release candidate** — the recomputation boundary discussion moved from conversation into runnable tooling inside a single window. [tg:tawg:5421]

> **Core/domain-adapter architecture confirmed against prior shipped work** — two contributors aligned on a design split already proven by decision-receipt v0.4, grounding the new verification direction in a concrete precedent. [tg:tawg:5428]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### attestation-architecture
_The self-attestation versus third-party recomputation boundary moved from open question to a collaboratively confirmed design pattern._

- Petchevere (@petchevere) **Shared** a longer-form writeup on Soma, an experimental agent marketplace handling natural-language tasks, surfacing the practical gap between self-attested claims and independently recomputable evidence — giving the group a grounded real-world case to reason against. [tg:tawg:5415]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Connected** Petchevere's framing directly to active verification thinking, articulating why the boundary between third-party-recomputable and self-attested behaviour matters for Trustless infrastructure. [tg:tawg:5418]
- Baby Blue Viper **Contributed** a precedent from decision-receipt v0.4, explaining that its core binds only a key to salted commitments without embedding domain meaning — an already-shipped example of the design separation the group was converging on. [tg:tawg:5426]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Proposed** applying the same core/domain-adapter split to the verify stack, keeping the core responsible for evidence identity, binding, and recomputation while domain adapters define what specific assertions mean — advancing the design from discussion to a clear structural proposal. [tg:tawg:5427]
- Baby Blue Viper **Confirmed** that decision-receipt v0.4 already shipped this exact pattern, anchoring the proposal in working code and giving the group a firm foundation for the verify stack. [tg:tawg:5428]

### receiptos-verify
_Concrete verification tooling progressed from audit follow-up to an initial public release._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Shipped** recompute-kit #65 as the F05 system-audit follow-up, closing a confirmed gap across five mutation harnesses and the encode fault controls — turning a real audit finding into addressed tooling. [tg:tawg:5413]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Published** the first experimental release candidate of receiptos-verify, translating the day's recomputation boundary discussion into an artifact the group can examine, test, and build on. [tg:tawg:5421]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Signaled** intent to refine receiptos-verify toward integration with the broader Trustless stack, moving it from a standalone experiment toward shared infrastructure for the group. [tg:tawg:5423]

### ERC-8183
_External escrow usage data landed on the public specification thread._

- agenticfinancegraph **Shared** a usage measurement from their transaction ledger showing how an ERC-8183-style escrow operates in practice — contributing external evidence the group can draw on when refining escrow settlement design in the specification. [Magicians #27902/424](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/424)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**
- Whether receiptos-verify's proposed core/adapter split could be formalized as a shared interface pattern across Trustless verification tooling
- How Soma's real-world attestation gaps might connect to ERC-8183 escrow settlement requirements

### ✅ **TODOs**
- Review the receiptos-verify experimental release candidate and provide feedback on the core binding and recomputation design
- Examine the ERC-8183 escrow usage measurements and consider their implications for open specification questions

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A real-world agent-marketplace writeup landed, sparked a cross-contributor architecture debate, and closed with a release candidate shipped and a design split confirmed from prior work — the whole loop from problem statement to tooling ran inside a single window.
>
> When the best answer to a design question turns out to be "we already shipped it," the stack is clearly working — now let's see how fast the next loop closes! 🚀
